findings.title: Role rights, role settings and employee edits have no hierarchy check: self-escalation to Admin
findings.problem: updatePageRights and update (designation.service.ts:449, 74) write any role, the caller's own and Admin's included, and grant rights the caller lacks. updateOnRoleEmployee (employee.service.ts:311) changes any employee's username, password and role with no level check; hasHigherDesignation is only used by one LOS step. Eve with DESIGNATION_PAGE edit gave her role EMPLOYEE_MAIN edit; with DESIGNATION_MAIN edit she set her role to level 1.
findings.impact: Any user given one of these pages can become Admin, raise own waiver/payment limits or reset the Admin password. With F23 (open employee import) it is a full takeover path.
findings.fix: Refuse writes to the caller's own role and to equal or higher roles/employees (hasHigherDesignation, allowEqual=false); refuse granting rights the caller lacks; audit every rights change.
findings.attentionNote: Found in Adam/Eve test run P5 T6

findings.title: External API credentials returned in plain text to anyone with External APIs view

Aadhaar, PAN, eSign, Credit Bureau, Bank Account. DB is a production copy, so keys may be live.
findings.impact: Holders of the page or a stolen session can call paid KYC/eSign/bureau services as the company and decrypt data under the encryption key.
findings.fix: Never return secret values: return set/not-set and last 4 characters; keep PUT for replacement; rotate keys that were exposed.
findings.attentionNote: Found in Adam/Eve test run P5 T6

findings.title: The send lock holds a database connection for the whole send, which can freeze the pool
findings.problem: The lock transaction stays open while createFinnauxEsignRequest renders the PDF, calls Finnaux and saves the row, and those steps run their own queries on other pooled connections. If as many sends (including double clicks, since each waiting click also holds a connection) are running as the pool has connections, every connection is held by a waiting transaction and none is left for the inner queries.
findings.impact: The sends and every other API request that needs a database connection hang, because the driver has no wait limit, until the server is restarted. Reproduced with a pool of 2: two concurrent sends stayed stuck after 5 seconds. The pool is DATABASE_POOL_MAX (10 locally), so it takes about 10 concurrent sends or double clicks.
findings.fix: Keep the lock short: inside one quick transaction take the lock, re-check the status and mark the document ESIGN_PENDING, then commit; do the PDF render and Finnaux call outside any transaction, and put the previous status back if Finnaux fails. A cap on concurrent sends below the pool size is a smaller alternative.
findings.resolvedNote: The lock transaction now only claims the document (select, check, mark ESIGN_PENDING) and the PDF render and Finnaux call run outside any transaction, with the claim undone on failure (apps/finnaux-api/src/los/loan-application/esign/esign.service.ts:174-196, 644, 727).

findings.title: A REVOKE or RESEND reply of SUCCESS marks the document signed
findings.problem: runFinnauxEsignAction maps data.status the same way for every action, and SUCCESS maps to ESIGNED_SUCCESS. If Finnaux answers a revoke or resend with data.status SUCCESS (meaning the action worked), the document is saved as signed with esignedAt set.
findings.impact: A revoked or re-sent agreement can show as signed in the loan application with no signed PDF behind it.
findings.fix: Map data.status only for STATUS. For REVOKE always store ESIGNED_FAILURE. For RESEND_INVITATION leave the stored status unchanged.

findings.title: Pending check is not atomic, so two creates can both reach Finnaux
findings.problem: The pending check reads the row, then calls Finnaux, then upserts. Two clicks at once both pass the check and both create a Finnaux request; the second overwrites the first session.

findings.fix: Lock the document row (select for update in a transaction) or set ESIGN_PENDING before calling Finnaux and roll back on failure.

findings.title: Including closed cases drops every open loan
findings.problem: buildLoanPortfolioFilter builds openLoanFilters, returns them only when includeClosedCases is false, and otherwise returns and(...closedLoanFilters). The previous or(open, closed) is gone, so with includeClosedCases=true the open filters are built and thrown away.
findings.impact: A report generated with 'include closed cases' contains only closed loans. The live portfolio is missing from the file submitted to the bureau, and the grid shows the wrong set.
findings.fix: Return or(and(...openLoanFilters), and(...closedLoanFilters)) when includeClosedCases is true, and import or again.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the filter returns or(open, closed) when closed cases are included at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/ucrf-report.service.ts:1372.

findings.title: Loans closed after the reporting date are reported as closed
findings.problem: The closed filter no longer has lte(loanCloseDate, reportingDate). It only requires loanCloseDate >= closedFromDate, so a loan closed after the reporting date matches.
findings.impact: For a back-dated reporting date, such a loan is written with a closed status code and a Date Closed later than the reporting date, although it was still open on that date.
findings.fix: Keep lte(loanApplicationsTable.loanCloseDate, reportingDateSql) in the closed filter next to the gte on closedFromDate.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: closed loans are bounded to closedFromDate through the reporting date, inclusive, at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/ucrf-report.service.ts:1363.

findings.title: NREGA id gets the string 'null' when last name is empty
findings.problem: row.lastName is typed string | null and is concatenated onto the NREGA number with +. A null last name produces '<card>null'.
findings.impact: The identifier written to the bureau file is corrupted for any customer with an NREGA card and no last name, and a long card number can be cut by the 30 character limit.
findings.fix: Append the last name only when it is present, for example number: row.nregaCard + (row.lastName ?? ''), or confirm with the spec that the name must be appended at all.
findings.evidence: ids.push({ type: TUDF_ID_TYPE.NREGA, number: row.nregaCard + row.lastName })
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the last name is appended only when present at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:141.

findings.title: Field 38 written empty when interest rate is null
findings.problem: formatInterestRate returns '' for a null rate and buildVarField turns that into the zero-length field '3800'. The field is also gated on noOfInstallments instead of on the rate.
findings.impact: Loans with installments but no IRR get an empty field 38 that the bureau can reject, and loans with a rate but no installment count never report it.
findings.fix: Gate the field on row.interestRate being present and non-null, not on noOfInstallments.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: field 38 is written whenever a rate exists, not only with installments, at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:378.

findings.title: New NREGA and CKYC master document ids look like placeholders
findings.problem: The two ids follow a sequential pattern unlike the neighbouring generated ids, and nothing else in the repo references them. If no master document row exists with these ids, the lookups always return null.
findings.impact: NREGA and CKYC numbers are silently never reported, which looks the same as customers having no such document.
findings.fix: Confirm both ids exist in the master documents table (or add the seed) and replace them with the real ids.
findings.resolvedNote: Marked resolved manually
findings.confirmedNote: Confirmed manually: NREGA and CKYC ids exist in the documents table (checked against the project database).

findings.impact: Clients generated from the API schema do not see the new Old Acc No column key, and oldAccountNo is still sent as a duplicate.
findings.fix: Add oldAccountNumber to the DTO and drop the unused oldAccountNo, or keep the old key in the column list.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the DTO now declares oldAccountNumber at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/dto/ucrf-consumer-grid-row.dto.ts:85.

findings.title: Grid account type lost its default while the file keeps it
findings.problem: The grid now shows row.cibilAccountTypeCode as is, but the TUDF builder still writes (row.cibilAccountTypeCode ?? '05').padStart(2, '0') at tudf-file.builder.ts:346.
findings.impact: For a product with no CIBIL type the grid shows a blank account type while the submitted file says 05, so what the user reviews differs from what is sent.
findings.fix: Use the same default and padding in the grid, or remove the default from the file builder.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the grid applies the same 05 default and two-digit padding at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/lib/consumer/ucrf-consumer-grid.mapper.ts:90.
